evidence: decorative_mascot: In seg3:start, seg3:mid, seg3:end and seg4 Data just stands on top of the left circle, doing nothing tied to the 127% vs 195% stat. In seg0 and seg2 he stands on a ladder and points at the bar after it grows. He does not cause it.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start, mid and end show two identical discs, both labelled '127%' and 'Billionaire wealth'. The narration says the S&P 500 grew 195%, but that number and its label appear nowhere. The scene looks the same through seg4 and the payoff.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison machine got the billionaire series in both slots, so the S&P 500 value (195%) and its label were never bound. Because of that the video's central claim, that most of the growth is just stocks, is visually contradicted: the two discs are equal.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Bind the second slot to 'S&P 500' = 195% so the two forms differ visibly in size (195 vs 127). Give the scene a subject-made picture, for example a stack of billionaire money next to a taller stock-ticker tower, where Data pours or stacks stock certificates to make the S&P side grow past the wealth side. Use dark ink for the numbers so they read on the teal.
